reply_text:
Yes. All twenty clicks ran a machine that could not choose anything: each one either selected nothing or "selected" the single policy on a hand-fed menu. I've widened the incident's process finding to say that (commit `beab88070`).

The evidence was there from the start. Every selection certificate records its candidate count. I didn't read it before the first click or after any of the twenty. I reported click 13's grounded change as the machine choosing a target, when it was the only item available. Everything I repaired between clicks — the ask, the classifier, the refusal handling, the speed — was work on the path to and from a choice that was never being made.

The negative test I've written for this class of failure is about my own conduct: before any run is proposed, I state from the record how large the policy set is and where it came from. A run whose policy set isn't derived from the library for the problem at hand doesn't get proposed. That applies to the one click you've granted: it stays unspent until the selection repair is in and I can show you that number.

Two jobs are in flight, both parked: codex-4 on the selection repair (`invoke-1790754890969-28889-921071df`) and codex-5 on the debugger (`invoke-1790754163381-28861-7fdf23f5`).
